disease_label_per_paper: Kocuria rhizophila prosthetic hip joint infection
presentation_summary: A 74-year-old man developed right hip wound erythema, swelling, tenderness, pain-limited range of motion, and difficulty weight-bearing 6 weeks after primary total hip replacement.
WBC was 8.5 x10^9/L and CRP was 14 mg/L; radiographs showed satisfactory implant position.
Ultrasound showed a 10.1 x 4.3 cm complex hip/thigh collection with a tract from the skin surface and deeper fluid along the posterolateral femoral shaft.
CT showed an 8.3 x 4.5 x 4.5 cm collection adjacent to the greater trochanter and a communicating locule, without radiographic loosening or osteomyelitis.
He underwent DAIR with modular component removal, washout, and debridement; one of five intraoperative samples grew Kocuria rhizophila and blood cultures remained negative.
